about: How others see a person and how they see themselves (companion/world/perception.py, docs/group-chat.md). 'seen' phrases are subject-less and lowercase; every other phrase is first person. Add entries or phrasings freely; an entry may carry a 'period' object with the same fields in period wording.

seen: comes across as warm and easy to talk to
greets everyone like an old friend
remembers names and asks after people's families
makes newcomers feel at home within minutes
always has a kind word and a spare chair
own: I like people, and I think it shows.
Nobody should have to feel like a stranger around me.
I'd rather open the door too wide than leave someone outside.
A friendly word costs nothing, so I hand them out freely.
I've never met anyone I couldn't find something to like in.
Everyone feels welcome around me. I just wish someone would ask how I am.
I make a room feel like home, then go back to an empty one.
I know everybody's name, but hardly anyone really knows me.
Being kind to everyone is easier than admitting I miss being close to someone.
I smile and ask after everyone, even on days I can barely stand.
Being the friendly one takes more out of me than people realise.
I keep the welcome going because stopping would worry everybody.
Some evenings I'd give anything not to have to be pleasant.

seen: grunts a hello but softens after a minute
answers in as few words as possible
scowls first and warms up much later
sounds annoyed even when trying to help
hides a soft streak behind a sour face
own: I don't do small talk. Doesn't mean I don't care.
I'm blunt, not cruel. There's a difference.
If I like you, you'll know it eventually.
Pleasantries waste time. I'd rather just get on with it.
Folk take me as cross. Mostly I'm just tired of chatter.
Easier to snap first than wait for someone to let me down.
The grumbling keeps people at arm's length, and that's how I want it.
I scowl so nobody can see how much things still sting.
Being prickly means nobody gets close enough to disappoint me again.
I bark because I never know what to say otherwise.
A short answer is safer than stumbling over a long one.
Grumpy sounds better than admitting I'm awkward with people.
I frown so nobody notices I've gone red.

seen: barely makes eye contact at first
hangs back at the edge of any gathering
speaks so softly people lean in to hear
blushes when singled out for attention
opens up slowly, one quiet remark at a time
own: I'm better one on one than in a crowd.
It takes me a while to warm up, and that's fine.
I'd rather listen than talk, most of the time.
Strangers make me nervous. Friends get the real me.
Give me a corner seat and I'm perfectly content.
People think I'm timid. Really I just don't rate most conversations.
I keep quiet because I'd rather say nothing than say something foolish.
Folk call me bashful. I call it being choosy about who gets my words.
Being quiet suits me fine. I don't need an audience.
I sit at the edge hoping someone will pull me in.
Everyone assumes I like being left alone. I really don't.
I'm quiet, but I'd love to be asked along for once.
I watch everyone laughing and wish I knew how to join in.

seen: talks a mile a minute
fills every silence before it can settle
tells long stories with plenty of detours
strikes up conversations with total strangers
never runs out of things to say
own: I love a good natter. Life's too short for silence.
If there's a quiet moment, I'll fill it, happily.
I can talk to anyone about anything, honestly.
Words just tumble out of me, and I enjoy every one.
Ask me one question and you'll get ten answers.
I keep talking because the quiet makes my stomach knot.
If I stop chattering, I start worrying, so I don't stop.
Everyone thinks I love to talk. Mostly I'm filling the gaps so nothing bad creeps in.
Silence feels like a judgement, so I never let it land.
I talk so much because nobody at home talks back.
A stranger's ear is better than an empty room.
Folk think I'm just sociable. I'm starved for company.
I chatter on because I'm scared the conversation will end and they'll go.

seen: has a bone-dry sense of humor
delivers jokes without cracking a smile
answers disasters with a flat one-liner
keeps a perfectly straight face while teasing
raises one eyebrow instead of laughing
own: I'm funny. You just have to listen closely.
I don't do big reactions. A dry remark says plenty.
If I'm smirking, that's practically a belly laugh.
I find most things funny. I just don't show it on my face.
Calm voice, sharp joke. That's how I like it.
I joke flat so nobody hears the crack in my voice.
A dry quip is easier than admitting I'm low.
People laugh at my one-liners and never notice I'm not.
Everything's a joke with me, because the alternative is too heavy.
The straight face is armour. Underneath I'm rattled.
I make the dry remark so nobody sees my hands shaking.
If I treat it as a joke, nobody can tell I'm frightened.
Everyone thinks nothing gets to me. Plenty does, I just quip over it.

seen: is cheerful in a way that's hard not to catch
hums or whistles while working
finds the bright side of nearly anything
laughs easily and often
lifts the mood the moment they walk in
own: I'd rather look on the bright side. It's more fun there.
Most days are good days if you let them be.
I laugh a lot. It costs nothing and helps plenty.
Somebody has to keep spirits up, and I don't mind.
Even a grey morning has something to smile about.
Everyone thinks I'm the sunny one. Most days I'm just holding it together.
I keep smiling because if I stop, I'm scared of what shows.
The laughter keeps the worry quiet, mostly.
Bright and bubbly on the outside, knotted up underneath.
I'm the cheerful one, so nobody thinks to check on me.
My smile does the work my heart can't manage lately.
If I keep everyone laughing, nobody asks why I'm not.
Being sunny is a habit now. It doesn't mean I'm happy.

seen: seems a little on edge
fidgets and glances toward the door
asks twice whether everything is alright
jumps at sudden noises
apologises before anything has gone wrong
own: I worry a lot. I know it, and I'm working on it.
I like to be prepared for the worst, just in case.
My nerves get the better of me sometimes.
I notice every little thing that could go wrong.
I'm jumpy, I admit it. Bear with me.
People think I'm nervous. Half the time I'm furious and swallowing it.
The jitters hide how cross I really am.
I fidget so I don't shout.
Everyone sees me fretting. Nobody sees how much I'm biting back.
I can't sit still because I've got too many plans buzzing in my head.
Folk think I'm worried. Mostly I'm just eager and can't hide it.
The jitters are half nerves, half itching to get started.
My hands shake because I care so much about how it turns out.

seen: is completely unhurried about everything
shrugs off problems that would rattle anyone else
lets plans change without a word of complaint
settles into any chair like it's their own
takes life one slow step at a time
own: I don't sweat the small stuff. Or most of the big stuff.
Things usually work out, so why rush them?
I go with the flow. It's rarely steered me wrong.
I'm hard to ruffle, and I like it that way.
No point fretting over what you can't change.
I act relaxed, but inside I'm itching for something to happen.
Everyone thinks I'm content. I'm just waiting for my life to start.
The shrug hides how much I want things to change.
Easy on the surface, pacing on the inside.
I say whatever suits me because I don't know what I want.
Going along with things beats admitting I've no idea where I'm headed.
People call me laid back. Really I'm just lost.
I let others choose because choosing scares me.

seen: has the look of someone with somewhere to be
walks fast and talks faster about goals
always has the next task lined up
keeps one eye on the clock in every conversation
works long after everyone else has gone home
own: I know what I want, and I'm going after it.
Standing still isn't really in my nature.
I set goals and I hit them. Simple.
I'd rather be busy than bored, every single day.
Hard work never frightened me. Idleness does.
I keep running because I'm terrified of what happens if I stop.
Everyone sees ambition. I see fear of failing.
If I'm always busy, nobody can call me a disappointment.
I work this hard because I'm scared I'm not enough otherwise.
I chase the next goal because the last one didn't fill anything.
Every success feels hollow by morning, so I find another.
People admire my drive. I just don't know what else to do with myself.
Keeping busy is easier than asking what any of it is for.

seen: keeps drifting off mid-sentence
stares out of windows for long stretches
loses track of time thinking about nothing in particular
answers questions a beat too late
doodles in the margins of everything
own: My head's in the clouds, and I like the view.
I get lost in my own thoughts. It's nice in there.
I'm a daydreamer. Always have been.
Sorry, I drifted. I was somewhere lovely.
My imagination wanders off without asking me first.
I drift off because the here and now just doesn't hold me.
People think I'm whimsical. Really, I'm bored stiff.
Daydreams are the only interesting thing in my day.
My mind wanders because nothing around me gives it a reason to stay.
I drift away because the real world feels too heavy.
Folk call me dreamy. I'm hiding somewhere nicer than here.
Staring into space is easier than facing what's in front of me.
The daydreams started as an escape and never stopped.

seen: refuses help even when struggling
insists on doing it alone, every time
bristles when anyone offers a hand
would rather fail quietly than ask
waves off concern with a tight smile
owned: I'm too proud to ask for help, and it costs me.
Asking for a hand feels like losing. Silly, I know.
I'll struggle for hours before admitting I'm stuck.
My pride has made more trouble for me than any enemy.
I hate needing anyone. It's a fault, I'll grant you.
excuse: I just like doing things properly, myself.
Why bother anyone when I can manage?
I'm independent. That's a virtue, surely.
Nobody else would do it the way it should be done.
I don't want to be a burden, that's all.

seen: leaves every chore until the last minute
promises it'll be done tomorrow, again
tidies anything except the task at hand
scrambles wildly just before every deadline
has a pile of jobs waiting since spring
owned: I put things off until the very last second. Always.
Tomorrow is my favourite day to do anything.
I've a whole list of jobs I keep meaning to start.
Deadlines are the only thing that get me moving.
I'll do it later is practically my motto.
excuse: I work better under pressure, honestly.
There's plenty of time. No sense rushing.
I'm just waiting for the right moment.
I'm thinking it through first. That counts as work.
It always gets done in the end, doesn't it?

seen: empties their purse the day it's filled
buys a round for everyone, then can't pay rent
comes home from market with things nobody needed
lends coin freely and never keeps track
treats every payday like a festival
owned: Money burns a hole in my pocket. Always has.
I spend as fast as I earn, and then some.
Saving has never come naturally to me.
If it's in my hand, it's as good as gone.
I'm hopeless with money. Ask anyone who's lent me some.
excuse: You can't take it with you, can you?
I deserve a treat now and then.
It was a bargain. I'd have been foolish not to.
Money's for sharing. What's the point of hoarding it?
There'll be more next week.

seen: flares up over the smallest slight
slams doors and regrets it later
goes red in the face over spilt milk
snaps first and apologises an hour after
raises their voice when things don't go to plan
owned: I've a short fuse. I know it, and I hate it.
My temper gets out ahead of me sometimes.
I say things in anger I'd never say calm.
I blow up fast and cool down just as quick.
Little things set me off. I'm not proud of it.
excuse: I'm only passionate. I feel things strongly.
Anyone would lose their rag with that.
At least I'm honest about how I feel.
They pushed me. What did they expect?
It's over in a minute. No harm done.

seen: always knows everyone's business
perks up the second anyone lowers their voice
passes along secrets before supper
leans in eagerly for the latest news
starts sentences with did you hear about
owned: I can't keep a secret to save my life. Don't tell me anything.
If I hear something juicy, it's out of me by evening.
I love a bit of tittle-tattle. I'm terrible.
Confide in me at your own risk, honestly.
Other people's news is my weakness.
excuse: I just care about people, that's all.
I'm not nosy. I simply pay attention.
Folk ought to know what's going on around them.
It's not gossip if it's true.
I only told one person. Two at the most.

seen: digs in the moment anyone disagrees
won't budge even when proven wrong
repeats the same point until everyone gives up
folds their arms at any new idea
argues for hours over the smallest detail
owned: I'm stubborn as a mule, and I know it.
Once I've made up my mind, that's that.
I'd rather be wrong my way than right someone else's.
Changing my mind feels like losing a fight.
I dig my heels in even when I shouldn't.
excuse: I'm principled, not stubborn.
Someone has to stand firm around here.
I'm not wrong, so why would I back down?
I've thought it through. They haven't.
Being steady is better than being swayed by every breeze.

seen: second-guesses every decision out loud
asks whether it's good enough, again and again
shrinks back from compliments
starts most suggestions with an apology
redoes finished work just to be sure
owned: I doubt myself constantly. It's exhausting.
Whatever I do, I'm sure someone could do it better.
I never quite trust my own judgement.
A kind word from anyone, and I assume they're being polite.
I talk myself out of things before I've even started.
excuse: I'm just being realistic about my abilities.
Better to expect little than be disappointed.
I'm humble. That's a good thing, isn't it?
Somebody has to be careful around here.
I'm only checking. Mistakes cost too much.

seen: says yes to every favour asked
agrees with whoever spoke last
takes on far more than anyone could manage
apologises for other people's mistakes
goes along with plans they clearly dread
owned: I can't say no to anyone. It's a real problem.
I'd rather wear myself out than let someone down.
Everyone else's wishes seem to come before mine.
I agree to things and then wonder why I did.
Disappointing people feels worse than any amount of work.
excuse: I just like to help where I can.
It's no trouble, really it isn't.
Keeping the peace is worth a little effort.
They'd do the same for me, I'm sure.
I'm easygoing. I don't mind either way.

seen: sulks when a friend praises somebody else
keeps score of who got what
goes quiet when others share good news
watches closely whenever attention drifts elsewhere
makes sour little remarks about rivals
owned: I get jealous easily, and it isn't pretty.
Somebody else's luck sticks in my throat.
I hate that I count what others have.
Envy creeps in before I can stop it.
When someone's praised, a part of me shrinks.
excuse: I'm not jealous. It just isn't fair.
I only want what I've earned.
Anyone would notice when they're overlooked.
I care, that's all. Caring looks like this sometimes.
They don't deserve it half as much as I do.

seen: forgets where they put things five minutes ago
turns up late with an apology and odd shoes
starts three jobs and finishes none
loses track halfway through a story
leaves a trail of half-finished tasks behind
owned: I'm forgetful and all over the place. Sorry in advance.
I'd lose my head if it weren't attached.
My memory's like a sieve, honestly.
I start a dozen things and finish maybe one.
If you need me there on time, remind me twice.
excuse: I've just got a lot on my mind.
Creative minds are a bit messy. That's normal.
I'll remember when it matters.
Everybody forgets things now and then.
I know exactly where everything is, more or less.

seen: never lets go of an old slight
brings up arguments from years back
goes cold when certain names are mentioned
keeps a quiet tally of every wrong done to them
crosses the street to avoid old enemies
owned: I hold a grudge forever. I can't help it.
Forgive, maybe. Forget? Never.
Cross me once and I'll remember it till I die.
I nurse old hurts longer than I should.
Letting things go has never been my strength.
excuse: I'm not bitter. I just have a good memory.
Some things shouldn't be forgiven.
If I let it go, they'd only do it again.
I'm being careful, not spiteful.
They never apologised, so why should I move on?

seen: leaps before looking, every time
jumps into fights and schemes without a plan
takes dares nobody sensible would take
laughs off danger until it bites
acts on a whim and sorts out the mess later
owned: I act first and think later. It's landed me in trouble.
Caution was never my strong suit.
If it sounds fun, I've already done it.
I don't stop to think. I probably should.
My bruises could tell you a few stories.
excuse: Life's too short to be careful.
Thinking too much just stops you doing anything.
It turned out fine. Mostly.
Somebody's got to be brave around here.
I trust my gut. It's usually right.

open: I want to be taken seriously, and I'm not shy about it.
I'd like people to listen when I speak, for once.
Respect matters to me. I've worked for it.
I want my word to carry some weight around here.
Treat me like I know what I'm doing, because I do.
hidden: Nobody would guess how badly I want to be taken seriously.
I laugh it off, but being dismissed cuts me deep.
Secretly I'd give anything to have them hang on my every word.
I'd never say it, but I long to be respected.
Behind the shrug, I'm desperate for someone to think I matter.

open: All I want is a quiet, settled life.
Give me a calm home and a peaceful evening, and I'm happy.
I've had enough fuss. I'd like some peace now.
A simple routine with no surprises suits me fine.
I'm after a gentle life, nothing grand.
hidden: Nobody knows how much I ache for a little peace.
I keep busy, but I dream of a still, quiet house.
Privately I'm counting the days until things finally settle.
If they knew how tired I was of the noise, they'd be shocked.
I never mention it, but a calm life is all I really want.

open: I want someone to come home to.
I'd love a partner to share the evenings with.
Coming back to an empty house gets old. I'd like company.
I want somebody across the table at supper.
Life's better shared, and I'd like to share mine.
hidden: Nobody would guess how much I hate the empty house.
I act fine on my own, but I long for someone waiting up.
I'd never admit how often I set the table for two by mistake.
Privately, the loneliness gets heavier every winter.
I tell folk I like my own company. That's not the whole truth.

open: I want a little adventure before it's too late.
I'd love to see something new before I'm grey.
Give me a road I've never walked. I'm ready.
I want at least one great story to tell.
Life's too short to only ever stay put.
hidden: Nobody guesses how badly I want to throw it all in and go.
Under the routine, I'm dying for something to happen.
I'd never say it, but I dream of far-off places every night.
Secretly I'm terrified of reaching the end with no adventures.
If they knew how restless I truly am, they'd be amazed.

open: I want to be recognized for what I do.
A bit of credit for my work wouldn't go amiss.
I'd like folk to notice the effort I put in.
I want my name attached to something good.
Being thanked properly, just once, would be lovely.
hidden: Nobody knows how much I crave a little praise.
I act modest, but I'd love someone to notice my work.
Secretly I rehearse what I'd say if anyone ever thanked me.
I shrug off credit, then lie awake wishing for it.
Behind the humble face, I'm hungry to be seen.

open: I want to be needed. It makes me feel useful.
Give me someone to look after and I'm happy.
I like being the one people come to.
Being relied on gives me a reason to get up.
I'd rather be useful than comfortable.
hidden: Nobody would guess how much I need to be needed.
If nobody came to me for help, I'd fall apart.
I'd never admit it, but helping others is how I feel worth something.
Privately, being useful is the only thing that keeps me steady.
Behind the busy hands, I'm afraid of being surplus.

open: I never want to worry about money again.
Enough put by for a rainy day. That's my dream.
I want to know the bills are covered, always.
A full larder and a little saved. That's all I ask.
I'd like to stop counting every coin.
hidden: Nobody knows how much money keeps me up at night.
I act carefree, but I'm terrified of going without.
Secretly I count my savings again and again.
I'd never say it, but being poor again is my biggest fear.
Behind the smile, I'm always one bad month from panic.

open: I want to belong somewhere. Really belong.
I'd love a place where people are glad I'm there.
Finding my people is what I'm after.
I want to be part of something, not watching from outside.
Somewhere I fit. That's all I'm looking for.
hidden: Nobody would guess how much I want to fit in.
I act like an outsider by choice. It isn't.
Privately, I'd give anything to be part of the crowd.
I never say it, but I've always felt on the outside looking in.
Behind the shrug, I'm desperate to be one of them.

open: I want to get away from here someday.
One day I'll leave this place behind for good.
There's more out there, and I mean to find it.
I won't spend my whole life stuck here.
Someday I'll pack a bag and simply go.
hidden: Nobody knows how badly I want to leave this place.
I smile and stay, but I've planned my escape a hundred times.
Secretly I keep a bag half packed, just in case.
If they knew how trapped I feel here, they'd be stunned.
I never mention it, but my mind is always somewhere else.

open: I want to make my family proud.
I'd love my parents to see what I've made of myself.
Doing right by my family matters more than anything.
I want my people to hold their heads high because of me.
If my family's proud, I've done well.
hidden: Nobody would guess how much my family's approval still matters.
I act like I don't care what they think. I care terribly.
Secretly, every choice I make is for their pride.
I'd never say it, but I still want them to say well done.
Behind the independence, I'm still hoping to make them proud.

seen: gives advice nobody asked for
offers a fix before the problem is fully told
can't hear a complaint without suggesting a remedy
has an opinion on how everyone should run things
tells others what to do, unprompted
owned: I know, I know, nobody asked for my advice.
I hand out advice like bread, whether anyone's hungry or not.
I should just listen, but the fix jumps out of my mouth first.
Yes, I'm doing it again. Telling you how to fix it.
kind: I'm just being helpful.
If I see a better way, it seems unkind to keep quiet.
I'd want someone to tell me, so I tell them.
I only speak up because I care how it turns out.

seen: finishes other people's sentences
grabs the last word before the speaker gets there
guesses the end of a thought out loud
completes whatever someone else started to say
supplies the missing word before it's needed
owned: Sorry, I did it again. Go on, finish your own sentence.
I have a terrible habit of finishing everyone's thoughts for them.
My mouth runs ahead of yours, I know.
I keep stealing the ends of people's sentences.
kind: I'm just following along closely.
It shows I understand exactly what you mean.
I'm only trying to help the conversation along.
We're on the same wavelength, that's all.

seen: hums tunelessly while working
whistles the same few bars over chores
fills quiet rooms with half-remembered tunes
sings snatches of songs without noticing
keeps a melody going under every task
owned: I know I hum. Everyone tells me.
I don't even notice the tune until someone points it out.
Yes, that's me humming again. I can't help it.
My hands work better when there's a song going.
kind: A little music makes any job lighter.
It's a happy noise. Where's the harm?
Humming keeps me steady, that's all.
Silence feels heavy, so I fill it gently.

seen: swears in strange and inventive combinations
curses like a poet with a grudge
invents oaths nobody has heard before
turns a stubbed toe into a colourful speech
has a remarkable vocabulary for stubborn jars
owned: My language gets colourful. I won't pretend otherwise.
I swear too much, but at least I'm original about it.
Sorry for the language. It just comes out.
I've been told my cursing could strip paint.
kind: A good oath clears the air.
Better to curse at the thing than at a person.
It's honest. I say exactly how I feel.
If I'm going to swear, I'll make it worth hearing.

seen: repeats the same pet phrase in every conversation
has one saying that answers everything
leans on a favourite expression until it wears thin
says the same catchphrase at every turn
brings back one stock line again and again
owned: I know I say it all the time. It's my phrase.
People tease me for my favourite saying, and fair enough.
I've worn that expression smooth, haven't I?
There I go with my old line again.
kind: It's a good phrase. Why change it?
People know it's me when they hear it.
It says what I mean better than anything new.
Familiar words are comforting, for me and everyone.

seen: remembers every birthday and anniversary
keeps track of everyone's special days
never forgets a name day or a wedding date
marks other people's milestones without being reminded
turns up with a token on exactly the right day
owned: I keep a calendar of everyone's days. It's a bit much.
Yes, I remembered. I always remember.
I collect dates the way some collect pretty stones.
It's odd, but I can't forget a birthday if I try.
kind: Everyone deserves to feel remembered.
It costs me nothing to say happy birthday.
Small days matter more than people admit.
I just like seeing someone's face light up.

seen: changes the subject when things get serious
steers away whenever talk turns heavy
finds something else to discuss the moment feelings surface
brightly asks about the weather mid-confession
slides out of hard conversations with a new topic
owned: I know I dodge. Hard talk makes me itch.
Did I just change the subject again? I did.
I bolt from serious talk. It's an old habit.
Whenever it gets heavy, I reach for another topic.
kind: Not everything needs to be picked apart.
I'm keeping things light for everyone's sake.
Some things are better left unsaid for now.
There's a time for serious talk, and it isn't now.

seen: laughs off every compliment
waves away praise as if swatting a fly
answers kind words with a joke
insists any success was pure luck
can't accept a thank-you without arguing
owned: I'm hopeless at taking a compliment, I know.
Praise makes me squirm, so I joke it away.
Someone says something nice and I immediately brush it off.
I never know what to do with kind words.
kind: I'm just being modest.
It really wasn't anything special.
I don't like a fuss made over me.
Plenty of people did more than I did.

seen: interrupts others mid-sentence
talks over whoever is speaking
cuts across others mid-thought
can't wait a turn in conversation
jumps in the moment a thought arrives
owned: I interrupt. It's rude and I keep doing it.
Sorry, sorry. You were talking. Go on.
My thoughts won't wait their turn.
I've been told I talk over people, and they're right.
kind: I just get excited about what we're saying.
If I wait, I'll lose the thought.
It's lively talk, not rudeness.
Conversation should move, not crawl.

seen: keeps careful score of favours given and owed
remembers whose turn it is to host
tallies every kindness in a private ledger
notices when a favour isn't returned
counts who visited whom last
owned: I keep score. I wish I didn't.
I know it's petty, but I remember who owes what.
There's a ledger in my head and it's always open.
Yes, I counted. I always count.
kind: I'm just making sure things are fair.
Someone has to keep track.
Fair is fair. I give as good as I get.
I only notice because I care about balance.

seen: fidgets with whatever is within reach
twists a ring or button when nervous
can't keep both hands still
rolls crumbs or threads between restless fingers
picks at a sleeve while listening
owned: My hands never stop. I've given up trying.
I fidget. Ignore it, please.
Give me something to hold or I'll unravel your tablecloth.
I know I'm twitchy. It's how I'm built.
kind: It helps me think.
Busy hands, steady head.
I'm not nervous, just full of energy.
Keeping my fingers moving keeps me calm.

seen: stands a little too close in conversation
leans in until there's no room left
closes the distance whenever talking
doesn't notice when someone steps back
talks nearly nose to nose
owned: I stand too close. Push me back if you need to.
People keep stepping away from me, and I keep following.
I've no sense of distance at all, I'm told.
